reference.source: Williams Textbook of Endocrinology / Nelson Textbook of Pediatrics
clinicalPearls: An autosomal dominant syndrome caused by activating mutations in the RET proto-oncogene
Medullary thyroid carcinoma, arising from calcitonin-producing C cells, is the defining and most consequential feature
Phaeochromocytoma occurs in both MEN2A and MEN2B and must be excluded before any surgery
MEN2A additionally features primary hyperparathyroidism, whereas MEN2B features a marfanoid habitus and mucosal neuromas but not hyperparathyroidism
The specific RET codon mutation stratifies medullary thyroid carcinoma risk and guides the timing of prophylactic thyroidectomy
Calcitonin and carcinoembryonic antigen serve as tumour markers for medullary thyroid carcinoma
Genetic testing enables presymptomatic diagnosis and risk-directed preventive thyroid surgery in gene carriers
reference.pathophysiology: RET encodes a receptor tyrosine kinase important for the development of neural crest-derived tissues, including thyroid C cells and the adrenal medulla. Germline activating mutations drive constitutive kinase signalling that promotes proliferation, so C cells progress through hyperplasia to medullary thyroid carcinoma and chromaffin cells give rise to phaeochromocytoma. The particular mutated codon correlates with how aggressive and early the medullary carcinoma is, which underpins genotype-directed decisions about the age at which prophylactic thyroidectomy is undertaken. Distinct mutation patterns account for the differing feature sets of MEN2A and MEN2B.
additionalDifferentials: Sporadic or other hereditary phaeochromocytoma syndromes
Von Hippel-Lindau disease and neurofibromatosis type 1
additionalInvestigations: Serum calcitonin and carcinoembryonic antigen as medullary thyroid carcinoma markers
Plasma or urinary metanephrines to screen for phaeochromocytoma
Serum calcium and parathyroid hormone to detect hyperparathyroidism in MEN2A
Neck ultrasound and adrenal imaging for tumour localisation
Molecular genetic testing of RET with codon-level characterisation
redFlags: Unrecognised phaeochromocytoma before surgery risking a hypertensive crisis
Rising calcitonin indicating progressive or metastatic medullary thyroid carcinoma
Aggressive early-onset medullary carcinoma associated with high-risk RET mutations
Marfanoid features and mucosal neuromas in a child suggesting MEN2B needing urgent evaluation
reference.prognosis: Outcome is dominated by medullary thyroid carcinoma; presymptomatic diagnosis with genotype-directed prophylactic thyroidectomy can be curative, whereas late diagnosis with metastatic disease carries a poorer prognosis.
pitfalls: Operating on the thyroid without first excluding a phaeochromocytoma
Missing the diagnosis in apparently sporadic medullary thyroid carcinoma that is actually hereditary
Delaying prophylactic thyroidectomy beyond the window indicated by the RET genotype
Failing to offer cascade genetic testing to at-risk relatives
